jp: 京都[きょうと]までは新幹線[しんかんせん]で{あまり|av-degree}時間[じかん]がかかりません。
en: It doesn't take much time to get to Kyoto by Shinkansen.
why: あまり goes with a negative to mean not very much.

jp: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]は人[ひと]が{とても|av-degree}多[おお]くて、歩[ある]きにくかったです。
en: There were an awful lot of people in front of the station, and it was hard to walk.
why: とても means very, so it fits a crowd that makes walking hard.

jp: バスが来[こ]ないので、{少[すこ]し|av-degree}待[ま]ってください。
en: The bus hasn't come, so please wait a little.
why: 少し means a little, the natural amount in a polite request.
